newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends down after five days of gains.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends down after five days of gains.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed lower against the U.S dollar on Thursday, reversing its recent five straight days of gains on non-delivery-forward U.S. dollar buying and month-end greenback demand from importers, dealers said.
The local dollar ended at an intraday high of T$27.515, off from a T$27.570 low, against Wednesday's T$27.507 close.
Turnover through dealers was a heavy US$411 million.
Dealers noted active U.S. dollar buying from non-delivery-forward trade during most of the session, helping the downward corrections on the Taiwan dollar.
"Non-delivery-forward buying on U.S. dollars emerged right from the beginning, following the overnight rebound of the U.S. dollar overseas," said one dealer.
"Month-end U.S. dollar demand from importers also emerged as importers saw active U.S. dollar buying once the Taiwan dollar rose close to the T$27.50 level on Wednesday," he said.
But dealers said the Taiwan dollar's fall was offset in late trade to react to the U.S. dollar overseas, which had turned softer.
For Friday, a stable T$27.50-27.53 range was seen.
